chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Ubaydullah al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about an elderly man who is too weak to fast in the month of Ramadan, so he said: He should give charity in the form of feeding one poor person for each day.
ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for an elderly person who cannot fast in Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar establishes the fidya (compensation) for the elderly or chronically ill who cannot fast, requiring them to feed one poor person per missed day. It highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on accessibility in worship, where physical incapacity transforms the obligation from fasting to charitable sustenance, ensuring the spiritual benefit is maintained through economic support of the needy.
